## Which file do I need?

| You want to… | Download |
|---|---|
| Play straight away on any computer | **cognitive-terrain-0.17.html**, then double-click it to open in your browser |
| Read the rules | **Cognitive-Terrain-Field-Manual-0.17.pdf** |
| Run it for a group, build campaigns, see why it works | **Cognitive-Terrain-Practitioners-Manual-0.17.pdf** |
| Hear each week read aloud (optional) | the **Immersive Briefings** voice pack, on its own release: **voice-emma-1** |
| Install it like a normal program | **…-Setup.exe** (Windows), **…-macOS-AppleSilicon.zip** or **…-macOS-Intel.zip** (Mac), **…-Linux.tar.gz** |
| Host it on itch.io | **…-web.zip** |

The installers are not code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS warn on first
launch. **PLAYTEST-README.txt** explains how to get past the warning.

Two-player games work between any of these files, as long as both players
use version 0.17.

## What's new

- **White Cell for structured sessions.** A facilitator can now join a
  two-player game as a third person, the White Cell, who sees both sides and
  steers the exercise:
  - only when chosen: Blue starts a **NEW STRUCTURED SESSION · WITH WHITE
    CELL**; ordinary two-player games are unchanged;
  - codes go round a circle, Blue → Red → White Cell → Blue, and the White
    Cell joins with Red's first code;
  - once a week, after Red and before Blue, its console offers eight tabs:
    the situation (both sides' health, budgets, hidden facts and what the
    computer would play next), board changes, budget and moves, crises and
    new technologies, a breaking story, a ruling, a teaching note, and its
    own limits;
  - almost everything is point and click: click a node on the map to open
    it in the console, then one click shifts control, sets a status or
    plants a dormant narrative; budgets and moves are buttons too;
  - a story can carry a picture: browse for one, drop it or paste it, and
    it is shrunk to fit inside the code, so it travels by email or chat;
  - every change is listed with a preview of its effect before it is
    released, and nothing is secret: both players see a White Cell notice
    before Blue's turn;
  - a move that breaks the exercise's rules can be struck, with a reason;
    every copy rebuilds itself without it;
  - the debrief and its replay show every White Cell change and teaching
    note, week by week.
- **Manuals.** The Practitioner's Manual has two new pages on the White Cell
  (setting one up, the console, pictures and suggested injects) and is now
  18 pages. The Field Manual's two-player pages say what players see in a
  structured session.
- **New code format.** White Cell sessions add fields to the turn codes, so
  two-player codes work only between 0.17 builds. No other rule changes.
